audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows contradicted their own whys. Level 1 read Skill while whys[0] says 'I can walk up and contest the wave'; Level 2 read Jayce while whys[1] opens 'Even window'; Level 6 read Skill while whys[4] says his all-in 'outdamages my kit'; first item read Jayce while whys[5] says 'First item flips it back'; 2+ items read Jayce while whys[6] opens 'I run him down late'.
audit.why: The lane is a poke window bounded on both ends: Maokai wins level 1 and everything from first item onward, Jayce owns level 3 and level 6. The packet chart says exactly that and the mirror audit set its side to the same seven rows.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Maokai / Skill / Jayce / Skill / Jayce / Maokai / Maokai as one atomic group of matched full+content pairs, ratings moved to 7/5/5/4/3/7/7.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phase whys were boilerplate, and packet.defects notes no Jayce ability is ever named there.
audit.why: The spikes are numeric and legible: Shock Blast at 16s falling to 6s across six ranks, the stance swap on 6s whose first cannon hit cuts armour and MR, Thundering Blow at 20s, and Maokai's W dropping to 11s at first item.
audit.corrected: All seven rewritten with the real names and figures.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] and late both say Jayce 'has no dash'. He does — To the Skies! is the hammer-stance Q, a leap to an enemy, and the kit derives a dash flag on it.
audit.why: The conclusion the page draws from 'no dash' is still right, but for the wrong reason, and a player who reads 'no dash' will misjudge his engage range. The accurate version is stronger: his only leap travels TOWARD you, so it never escapes a root — it delivers him into one.
audit.corrected: Corrected in whys[6], late and phases[6].why, each restating it as a leap that only closes distance.
sources: enemyKit Q text: 'Hammer Stance: Leaps to an enemy', dash flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said the first attack after swapping to cannon form reduces the target's Armor AND Magic Resist, and nothing said Sap Magic's cooldown shortens each time an enemy spell strikes Maokai.
audit.why: The resistance cut is aimed precisely at the thing Maokai builds, which is why level 6 is his spike rather than a generic 'ultimate changes the math'. And the Sap Magic mechanic inverts the poke war: Jayce chipping you pulls your next heal forward, so eating measured poke is not the pure loss the page implies. The mirror audit called this its headline mechanic error.
audit.corrected: The resistance cut written into phases[4].why; the Sap Magic mechanic into phases[1].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shock Blast is tracked on every screen with no number, and Thundering Blow — the ability that actually breaks a Maokai commit — is never given one.
audit.why: Thundering Blow at 20s is the long window; Shock Blast at 6s late is not something you wait out at all. The page has the priority backwards.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with both, plus the 6s stance swap; tradeGood re-keyed to Thundering Blow being spent.

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Jayce contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours — one stance, no combo, and Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1. Walk up and contest with your melee body.

edits.before: W root is your engage AND your peel — spend it once per fight. Only take the trade when Jayce's Shock Blast is down.
edits.after: Even at 2: your W-Q lockdown exists but he can space it. Whoever lands first wins, and his poke speeds up your Sap Magic.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Jayce must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: His level: gated Shock Blast gains range and damage, and 600 poke against your 525 W means he chips you without a reply.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Jayce's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: His swing: stance swap is 6s and the first cannon hit cuts your armour AND MR, then Thundering Blow knocks you out of the trade.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Shock Blast's cooldown.
edits.after: It flips to you — Heartsteel HP eats the poke and your W is down to 11s. Chain roots now.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Jayce carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on you run him down: To the Skies! only jumps toward you, so once the root lands he has no way out of it.

edits.before: - Jayce Shock Blast: matchup-defining — His main poke. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Jayce Shock Blast: matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1 down to 6s, and an Acceleration Gate adds range and damage. Step up after it. - Thundering Blow: 20s, 240 range, knocks you off him. - Stance swap: 6s.

edits.before: W-root Jayce the moment his answer is down, Q-knockback the follow-up, and let brush saplings tax his every path.
edits.after: W-root him once Thundering Blow is spent — it is 20s at rank 1 — then Q him back and sapling the brush he escapes through.

edits.before: I run him down late — no dash means one W ends him, and saplings plus Nature's Grasp let me wall and collapse while his burst bounces off my resists.
edits.after: I run him down late — To the Skies! only leaps toward me, so one W ends him, and saplings plus Nature's Grasp let me collapse while his burst hits my resists.

edits.before: Past first item I reclaim this lane — my tank line and shorter W cooldown mean I survive his poke and chain roots, while his burst falls off into my resistances. Saplings (E) zone his farm and ward his escape brush, and Nature's Grasp (R) walls any retreat or sets up a dive. He has no dash, so once W connects he's dead; my job is to make every fight happen in W range and let the team collapse on the root.
edits.after: Past first item I reclaim this lane — my tank line and an 11-second W mean I survive the poke and chain roots, while his burst falls off into my resistances. Saplings (E) zone his farm and ward his escape brush, and Nature's Grasp (R) walls any retreat or sets up a dive. His only leap goes TOWARD me, so once W connects he's dead; make every fight happen in W range and let the team collapse on the root.

notes: packet.suspectNames flags "Sap Magic's" in wants.foe[2] as a probable wrong name — false positive, it is the correct name with a possessive. One thing I did not touch and the user may want to: the whole page tracks Shock Blast, but Shock Blast reaches 6 seconds at rank 6, which is not a cooldown anyone waits out. Thundering Blow at 20 seconds is the real punish window, and I put that into breakdown.cooldowns and tradeGood — but focus.text, loading, winCon, tldr and six report strings still tell the player to track Shock Blast. Retargeting focus.text to Thundering Blow would be the single highest-value follow-up on this page and it is a clean enum-adjacent swap.
